subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the recurring Windows CI smoke lane include both `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke`, or should the first native PowerShell coverage be narrower?
rationale: The direction fits test-infrastructure goals, but the selected commands and Windows runner cost are maintainer policy choices and the active candidate is not yet a proven landed fix.

options.title: Prove full command set
options.body: Keep both commands in scope, but land only after the exact Windows `pwsh` lane passes and the PR links this issue correctly.

options.title: Start narrower
options.body: Land native PowerShell coverage only for commands already proven stable, then track build-smoke coverage separately.

options.title: Defer recurring smoke
options.body: Keep the issue open but do not add recurring Windows PowerShell smoke until runner budget or release priorities justify it.

recommendation.title: Prove full command set
recommendation.body: Keep both commands in scope, but land only after the exact Windows `pwsh` lane passes and the PR links this issue correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent overlap across the CI workflow surface and the PowerShell-safe docs formatter work adjacent to this command set.
